newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ITT, Koor in Israel hotel venture.
newsitem.headline: ITT, Koor in Israel hotel venture.

text.p: ITT Sheraton said on Wednesday it had signed an agreement taking a stake in an Israeli hotel management company controlled by Koor Industries and that the two are now eyeing prospects in the Palestinian areas.

The joint venture company, to be called Sheraton Israel Ltd, will manage four hotels now operated by the Koor unit and a fifth hotel now under construction. By 1998, Sheraton Israel will have 2,100 rooms under management, the two partners said.

Robert Cotter, president of ITT Sheraton Europe, said ITT controls 51 percent of the joint venture and Koor 49 percent. He added that the two sides would set up "a fund for purposes of equity investment" in Israeli hotel projects.
He said Sheraton Israel would also explore developing business in the Palestinian areas.
"Sheraton Israel Ltd is quite interested in finding a Palestinian partner so that we can begin development of quality international hotels in the Palestinian territories," Cotter told Reuters.
He said Koor CEO Benjamin Gaon had been approached by Palestinian Authority President Yasser Arafat on the matter.

Cotter said he was "very optimistic" regarding the peace process, which many executives in the tourism industry see as a key for the further development of tourism in Israel and the Middle East. "We have a long-term commitment to the region," he said.
Sheraton Israel takes over from Koor's wholly owned Koor Hotels and Resorts hotels in Jerusalem, Tiberias, Eilat and the Red Sea, all of which will operate under the Four Points Pardise name.
The two sides said they are in talks to transfer management contracts ITT Sheraton has with a second Jerusalem hotel and another in Tel Aviv.

At a signing ceremony in Tel Aviv, Gaon said Koor had invested over $100 million in the tourism business, including acquisitions in an Israeli airline and car rental company. He said the Sheraton deal was in line with Koor's strategy of allying its operating units with multinationals.
